subject: The 3-date myth that kills romance
preview_text: Everyone thinks you need 3 new dates a week. We crunched 10,000 couples' data. The truth will surprise you.
body_paragraphs: What if I told you that planning three new dates a week is actually making your relationship worse? I know, it sounds crazy. Every article, every influencer tells you to keep things fresh. But here's the thing — we analyzed 10,000 couples on SoulPlan, and the ones who planned the most dates didn't feel more connected. They felt more exhausted. The spark wasn't dying from lack of ideas. It was drowning in too many. The couples who kept the magic alive? They averaged one intentional date every 10 days. Not three. One. And they didn't try to reinvent the wheel each time. They repeated the dates that already worked, with tiny tweaks.

Here's the proof: couples who used the same date twice in a month reported 40% higher emotional connection scores than those who constantly chased novelty. Routine isn't the enemy — it's the scaffold for deeper intimacy. The real killer is the pressure to be creative every single week. That pressure turns 'tonight' into a chore. And when date night feels like a chore, you stop feeling seen. You stop feeling wanted.

That's why we built the 'Tonight's Date' feature the way we did. One tap on a mood — cozy, adventurous, playful, healing — and you get one card. Not a list. Not a menu. One. Because the research is clear: less choice, more connection. The AI learns what you both love and serves the same favorites, with subtle variations, so you never have to start from zero. And when your partner receives that card, they see a full-screen moment that says 'I thought of you tonight.' No notification noise. Just a memory you're building together.

Open SoulPlan now. Tap 'Tonight's Date' once. See how one simple card feels like a secret you both share. P.S. — The couples who hit a 7-day streak using this feature? They stopped feeling burnt out. They started feeling seen again. That's the real myth buster.
